chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Duke Ellington's aloofness and calling Mingus king of the waltz
summary: Mingus has few real talks with Duke; a Yale scene with Max Roach, and Duke's Birdland compliment about his waltzes.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But Duke claimed that his mother spoiled him all the time, and what was the line he used to say, that she wouldn't let his feet touch the ground until he was ten years old. And yet, he was --
Everybody was there to help him, remember that?
Yeah, yeah.
(Unintelligible) go that way.
Yeah.
He went across the street, they said, turn left. I don't believe him.
I don't believe him, either. He was a hard man to know. He sort of kept himself aloof from the band. Did you ever get to have any serious talk with him about anything at all?
I tried. Most serious I ever got was (inaudible) Yale?
Yale --
(Unintelligible.)
That's right, there's some kind of Ellington fund there.
And Max Roach was cussing out his bass player.
Joe Benjamin?

Calling him faggot. Joe Benjamin. Very loud. And I looked at Duke and Duke looked at me and he had the greatest conversation with the eyes. Because he knew I was about to kill Max. And he was saying, no, don't do it.
Any conversation you can remember, aside from the one in the book, in words?

Yeah, in Birdland one night (unintelligible). He's so beautiful, he really is. He said, look, man, you stop telling me that. Say, you know you are. You're the king of the . That was Richard Strauss, and you're the king of the waltz in jazz, Charles Mingus. Say, you think I don't listen? I know what you're doing. That's the only time he ever (inaudible).
That felt pretty good, I bet.
Yeah. It struck me later when he said it.
What did he mean?
Well, I was the first one other than Ray Charles, with the same jazz beat on the upbeat of the waltz. And he (unintelligible) was doing, he heard it.
x Johann
Yeah. Yeah, he really listened, all right.

McPherson told me, in San Francisco, they were playing the Monterey -- he never heard that. He was at a party -- he came to a party and as soon as he walked in, he heard, who's that, who's that? That's Mingus. Mingus? You know. I (unintelligible) got to him a couple of times.
Yeah. Like, for example?
That time.
That time.
In Monterey.
Yeah.
And the waltzes.
